newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Giordano says fined HK$93 mln by China.
newsitem.headline: Giordano says fined HK$93 mln by China.

text.p: Giordano International Ltd said on Monday its subsidiaries in China received penalty notices in 1996 from the authorities totalling about HK$93.00 million for alleged import irregularities and breach of a business licence.
The company said it decided not to make any provision at this stage as the penalty notices were under appeal and it was not practicable to estimate the ultimate cost to the group.

Certain manufacturing units in China received penalty notices from the customs authorities, alleging the improper transfer of duty free equipment to other group companies and irregularities in the usage of raw material imports, it said.
"The penalties claimed by the authorities related to events that occurred over the five-year period from 1992 to 1996 and total approximately HK$85.00 million," Giordano said.
The sales office of a Giordano subsidiary in China also received a penalty notice in the amount of about HK$8.00 million for alleged breaches of a business licence, it added.

"The directors are confident that any loss that might arise, including any penalties, additional duties and related legal costs, would not adversely affect the stability of the group as whole," Giordano said.

The casual wear retailer has had setbacks with its expansion in China, which most analysts believe are at least partly linked to unflattering comments that company founder Jimmy Lai made about Chinese Premier Li Peng in an article in 1994.
